A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same functional-equivalence framework and synthetic compositional study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original GPT-2 experiments measuring generalization, data scaling, representation clustering, causal tracing and CoT effects, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds Mamba results for two-hop data scaling and NON-TREE generalization.

M1.justification: The coverage-determination algorithm in Appendix C, GPT-2 training procedure and CoT supervision remain unchanged. Mamba is added as an evaluated comparison architecture; the framework's renamed emphasis does not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic two-hop, parallel two-hop, three-hop and NON-TREE structures, five-hop CoT setting and partial-computation variant. Mamba uses existing tasks. Renaming OOD examples as out-of-coverage does not change their construction.

E2.justification: V2 adds Mamba alongside GPT-2 in the two-hop scaling comparison (Figure 5) and a new NON-TREE comparison (Figure 19). The existing GPT-2 variants and comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The added Mamba experiments introduce a four-layer, 256-dimensional configuration with learning rate 0.008. Its scaling evaluation is restricted to token sets of size at most 100 because of training instability. Existing GPT-2 splits, metrics, training settings and generalization thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The Mamba analyses test whether the scaling relationship and path-ambiguity failure extend beyond Transformers. Existing causal tracing, task and token-set ablations, optimization sensitivity checks and partial-computation analysis are retained; the latter moves from Appendix I to Appendix E.

E5.justification: Both versions retain fit R-squared reporting and the check that 75% of each estimated data threshold fails the generalization criterion. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seeds, empirical confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports a Mamba two-hop scaling exponent of 2.00 in Figure 5 and low NON-TREE ID accuracy in Figure 19. Table 2's GPT-2 exponents and the matched diagnostic results remain unchanged. These additions concern the new Mamba configuration.

T1.justification: V1 Result 5.1 and Appendix E present a lower-bound argument using balanced classes and an Erdős–Rényi approximation. V2 Theorem 6.1 and Appendix F introduce sufficient bounds for k=1 and k≥2, a worst-case lower bound for k≥2 under Assumption F.6, revised closure and graph definitions, and extensive Poissonization and random-intersection-graph derivations. The exponent 2.5−0.5/k is retained, but the mathematical claims, assumptions and supporting arguments change substantially.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion shift from a broad coverage-principle account of systematicity and variable binding toward defining and characterizing a specific pattern-matching mechanism. V2 newly claims a tight two-hop sample-complexity characterization and empirical support across Transformer and Mamba architectures.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's strong conclusion that none of the three proposed mechanisms solves variable binding and substantially reduces the accompanying discussion of binding, length generalization and ambiguous decompositions. It adds an interpretation of logical-negation failures, links to natural-language multi-hop data requirements, and an explicit variable-length limitation. These revise the applicability and explanatory scope beyond simple relocation.

D1.justification: Figure 5 and Appendix H.3 newly document Mamba's architecture, learning rate and vocabulary-size restriction. The detailed GPT-2 implementation recipe remains unchanged. The existing code link moves into a reproducibility statement without a substantive change in access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially repositions the contribution around defining and isolating pattern matching, reducing the earlier connectionism, binding and disentanglement discussion. New Poissonization and random-intersection-graph references, including Singer and Zhao et al., support the revised theory; Truong et al. and Yuekun Yao et al. support added practical interpretations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The results narrative is reorganized into Sections 5–8, the taxonomy is condensed into Section 9.2 and Appendix I, and the partial-computation appendix moves earlier. Reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added.

P2.justification: V2 adds a Mamba series to Figure 5 and a new comparison in Figure 19, updates coverage labels, and relocates v1 Figure 19 as Figure 15. Most existing plots and both tables retain their structure. Headers, headings, captions and theorem displays are reformatted.

improvement.justification: The clearer mechanism-specific scope and added Mamba checks provide useful gains in clarity and empirical support. However, the expanded theory does not cleanly resolve v1's heuristic justification: the proof of Lemma F.26 uses ln(1+u)−u <= −u^2/2+u^3/6, which fails at u=0.1. The new proof therefore still requires correction, limiting the overall quality gain.
